claims.statement: Visa's merchant guidance describes a formal dispute response in which merchants submit supporting transaction, shipping and communication evidence through the acquirer.
Visa publishes merchant guidance for Compelling Evidence and scheme-specific dispute management.

Visa CE3.0 requires two prior undisputed transactions from the same merchant, 120-365 days before the dispute, with at least two matching core data elements including IP address or device ID/fingerprint; cross-merchant transaction histories cannot be substituted for that rule.
Stripe and Adyen expose programmatic dispute evidence workflows, but access and submission remain controlled by the merchant's PSP account, API credentials and dispute-management roles.

Direct and adjacent incumbents already offer outcome-priced automation: Stripe Poland publishes Smart Disputes at 30% of won disputed amount, Chargeflow publishes 25% with 100+ integrations, and Justt states success-based pricing and 50+ PSP integrations.

An EU deployment must establish a GDPR lawful basis and honor purpose limitation and data minimization; pseudonymisation is a safeguard rather than automatic anonymisation, and a service provider that can affect payment-account-data security may still have PCI DSS scope even without directly storing account data.

Visa's VAMP combines fraud and dispute monitoring and excludes some pre-dispute resolutions and CE3.0-qualified fraud from its ratio, giving merchants and acquirers a current operational incentive to prevent and resolve disputes as well as to win representments.

contrary_evidence: Visa and existing payment providers already offer dispute tools, so a new entrant needs a vertical evidence source they do not control.
Stripe's Smart Disputes and Adyen's Disputes API already automate evidence assembly or submission inside the PSP that controls the transaction and dispute data.
Chargeflow and Justt already market end-to-end, success-priced, multi-PSP evidence automation and cross-merchant learning, so a generic cooperative is not differentiated.
Visa CE3.0 requires historical transactions from the same merchant; cooperative data from another merchant cannot itself satisfy that evidence rule.
Pseudonymisation reduces risk but does not by itself remove GDPR duties, and PCI DSS scope can extend to a provider that affects payment-account-data security.

economics.acquisition_route: UNVALIDATED: embed with acquirers, PSPs, vertical SaaS platforms and marketplaces that each serve many merchants; PSPs already operate their own dispute automation, so a partner must see measured incremental recovery or vertical evidence unavailable to its native product.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: UNVALIDATED: serve 500 merchants by year 3 and 5,000 by year 6, supporting founder equity plus retained cash above PLN 5m in years 5-7; no merchant funnel, dispute volume, incremental lift, margin or valuation evidence supports the path yet.
economics.founder_time: UNVALIDATED: 3 hours per day for one vertical and one PSP, then model and exception oversight; security, scheme changes and partner onboarding may exceed this before operations are delegated.
economics.gross_margin_basis: UNVALIDATED: automated evidence retrieval and document assembly, with analyst review only for high-value exceptions, plus as-yet-unpriced GDPR, security and possible PCI DSS obligations.
economics.payback: UNVALIDATED: partner integration paid back after 80 recovered disputes or 6 months; integration cost, dispute mix, win lift and retained success fee are not evidenced.
economics.pricing: UNVALIDATED: share of recovered dispute value plus channel revenue share. Current public references are 25% at Chargeflow and 30% for Stripe Smart Disputes in Poland, so pricing power requires incremental lift, proprietary vertical evidence or a materially better net-recovery decision engine.
economics.retention_or_repeat: UNVALIDATED: ongoing transaction flow and scheme deadlines create recurring events; merchant-specific labeled outcomes can improve evidence selection, while any cross-merchant learning must use a lawful, minimized design and cannot replace Visa's same-merchant CE3.0 history.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Merchant-specific labeled outcomes and, where lawfully minimized, aggregate reason-code and vertical evidence performance improve selection without using another merchant's transactions as CE3.0 evidence
fingerprint.customer: Digital-goods, subscription and ecommerce merchants reached through PSPs or vertical platforms
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: PSP, acquirer, marketplace and vertical-SaaS embedding
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Evidence retrieval, representment packet, ROI-based fight-or-accept decision and outcome reconciliation for a success fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The merchant or payment partner pays when the disputed funds are restored or a pre-dispute is resolved
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An issuer opens a card dispute or pre-dispute inquiry and the merchant has a finite response window

founder_fit: A one-vertical, one-PSP pilot can be tested before broad network or compliance build-out
risks: Built-in PSP and network products can copy or bundle the workflow
Cross-merchant data reuse may lack a lawful basis or violate purpose limitation
Pseudonymised device, IP, login or delivery attributes may remain personal data
Security and PCI DSS obligations may consume more capital and founder time than forecast
Partner sales and enterprise security review may be slow and socially demanding
Optimizing win rate instead of net recovery can destroy value when dispute and countering fees apply

structure.control_point: The normalized merchant-specific evidence graph linked to final dispute decisions and recovered transactions, plus lawful aggregate performance signals
structure.critical_dependency: Merchant or partner-granted PSP access, a GDPR-compliant and appropriately scoped security design, scheme-compliant evidence use, final outcome labels, and measurable lift over native PSP and incumbent tools

thesis: Start with one evidence-rich vertical and one PSP where the merchant can authorize API access to disputes, order or usage records and final outcomes. Generate reason-code-specific packets, decide whether to fight based on expected net recovery, submit through the merchant's payment provider, and charge only when funds are restored or a pre-dispute is resolved. Use each merchant's own transaction history for Visa CE3.0 and keep any cross-merchant learning to lawfully minimized aggregate evidence-performance signals; do not treat pseudonymisation as exemption from GDPR. The opportunity depends on demonstrating incremental recovery from vertical evidence that native PSP automation and established vendors do not already control.
title: Chargeback Evidence Cooperative
uncertainties: Legal basis for privacy-preserving cooperative learning
Net-recovery lift after dispute, countering, partner and success fees
Which vertical has proprietary evidence unavailable to Stripe, Adyen, Chargeflow or Justt
Whether a PSP, acquirer or vertical platform will authorize submission and outcome access
Controller-processor roles and compatibility of cross-merchant secondary use under GDPR
PCI DSS scope and cost for the exact data architecture
Merchant willingness to grant device, login, communication and fulfillment data access
Sales-cycle length and security-review burden for embedded distribution
Minimum dispute volume needed for reliable reason-code and vertical outcome models
